question: When may you enter a yellow criss-cross box junction to go straight ahead?
options: Whenever the traffic lights are green
Only when your exit road is clear
When the car ahead is still moving slowly
At any time if you signal
explain: Highway Code Rule 174 states you must not enter a box junction unless your exit is clear.

question: When are you allowed to stop inside a yellow box junction?
options: When turning right and waiting for oncoming traffic to clear
When queuing to go straight ahead
explain: Highway Code Rule 174 allows stopping in the box only when turning right and blocked by oncoming cars.

question: What problem happens if you enter a box junction without a clear exit?
options: You could block cross traffic when the lights change
Your tyres lose grip on the yellow paint
explain: Highway Code Rule 174 keeps box junctions clear so cross traffic is not trapped.

question: The traffic light is green, but cars are queued just past the box junction. What should you do?
options: Drive into the box so cars behind you can cross
Wait behind the junction until space opens beyond the box
Sound your horn to make the queue move
explain: Highway Code Rule 174 says you must wait before the box even on a green light if the exit is blocked.

question: What colour are the criss-cross lines of a box junction?
explain: Highway Code Rule 174 marks box junctions with yellow criss-cross lines.

question: If you want to go straight across a box junction, what must be clear first?
options: The exit road on the far side of the box
Nothing if the light is green
explain: Highway Code Rule 174 says your exit must be clear before entering a box junction.

question: Why do busy crossroads have yellow box junctions?
options: To stop queuing cars from blocking crossing traffic
explain: Highway Code Rule 174 keeps the centre of busy junctions clear for cross traffic.

question: What should you do if a car in front stops inside a box junction and leaves no room on the far side?
options: Wait behind the box line until space opens past the box
Drive onto the yellow lines behind them
explain: Highway Code Rule 174 requires waiting outside the box until your exit is clear.

question: You are turning right at a box junction. Your exit road is clear, but oncoming cars block your turn. May you wait in the box?
options: Yes, you may wait in the box to turn right
Only if you turn on hazard lights
explain: Highway Code Rule 174 makes a specific exception when turning right and waiting for oncoming traffic.

question: You are turning right at a box junction, and the road you want to turn into is jammed full. May you enter the box?
options: No, because your exit road is blocked
explain: Highway Code Rule 174 only allows waiting in the box if your exit road itself is clear.

question: If the traffic light is green but the exit past the box is full, what could happen if you enter?
options: You will be stuck in the box when the cross traffic gets a green light
explain: Highway Code Rule 174 prevents drivers getting trapped across live junctions.

question: At a box junction, you follow a tall van and cannot see if space is clear beyond the box. What should you do?
options: Hold back before the box until you can see your exit is clear
Follow the van closely into the box
Overtake the van inside the box
explain: Highway Code Rule 174 means never entering blindly when a tall vehicle hides the exit.

question: Which turning direction has the special exception to wait inside a yellow box junction?
options: Turning right (when only oncoming traffic stops you)
explain: Highway Code Rule 174 grants the exception only for right turns blocked by oncoming traffic.

question: Are half-box junctions sometimes painted on only one side of a T-junction?
options: Yes, to keep that side clear for turning traffic
No, they are always full squares
explain: Highway Code Rule 174 covers full and half-box yellow markings at busy junctions.
